exposure: ultrasound-guided Foley balloon catheter placement combined with dilation and curettage (D and C)
outcome: successful treatment (b-hCG levels to 0, absence of gestational sac and vascularity)
cohort: The study included 311 patients with imaging-confirmed cesarean ectopic pregnancies up to 8 weeks' gestation admitted to Tu Du Hospital.
finding: The ultrasound-guided Foley balloon catheter placement combined with D&C successfully treated 90.7% of patients with cesarean scar ectopic pregnancies.
followup_time: Follow-up was conducted until b-hCG levels reached 0 and absence of gestational sac/vascularity was confirmed, with factors measured 2 weeks after treatment, but no single overall duration is specified.
